risks.risk: PS4 model/revision is unknown; pricing depends heavily on CUH version and whether it’s a slim/pro/older model.

risks.risk: “Hacked” status may mean unstable firmware, bans, or missing/removed features; also affects resale value.
risks.proof: Photo/video of the system settings screen showing firmware version and whether it’s running custom firmware (or a boot/system info screen).
risks.if_unproven: Price as hacked/modified with potential issues (worst-case: reduced value).

risks.risk: The 6 games may not be included as discs/cases, or may not work (corrupt installs, wrong region, or licenses).
risks.proof: Photo/video of the in-console game library showing all 6 titles installed and playable, or photos of the actual disc cases/discs.

risks.risk: Ports may be faulty (HDMI/USB/controller ports), which can make the console unusable or require repair.
risks.proof: Video showing HDMI output to a TV and testing USB ports + controller charging/connection.
risks.if_unproven: Price as if ports may be unreliable (worst-case: treat as needing testing/possible repair).

risks.risk: Overheating risk can’t be confirmed without a stress test; fan/thermal paste issues are common in used consoles.
risks.proof: A short gameplay/benchmark session video (10–15 minutes) plus a screenshot/photo of any temperature/overheat warning (if shown).
risks.if_unproven: Price as if overheating is possible (worst-case: assume it may need cleaning/thermal paste).
